Nicknamed after a judge was told to tremble before God's authority by their founder, members of this group call each other Friends and reject creeds and hierarchical structures — which movement?

During the French Revolution, this period saw waves of public executions ordered by the Committee of Public Safety, with some historians dating its start to the Law of Suspects in September 1793 — what is this era known as?
Reign of Terror: 1793–1794 period of political violence during the French Revolution.
Elected in 1987 as the first South Korean president chosen by direct popular vote, this former army general had earlier helped his military academy friend seize power in a 1979 coup. Who is he?
Roh Tae-woo: President of South Korea from 1988 to 1993.
Born Rozbih Khwushbudhan and trained as a Zoroastrian magus, this companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad converted to Islam after meeting him in Medina — who was he?

Salman the Persian: Companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. Muhammad specifically said "Salman is part of my Ahl al-Bayt." In meetings with the other companions, he was often referred to by the kunya Abu ʿAbdullah.
Sparked by a succession crisis after King Frederick VII died heirless, Prussian and Austrian troops crossed into a Danish-controlled duchy in February 1864 — which 19th-century conflict?
Second Schleswig War: War between Denmark, Prussia, and Austria in 1864.

Formed in 2022 after a leadership split within a major Maharashtra party, this faction led by former chief minister Uddhav Thackeray was given a new 'Flaming Torch' symbol by India's Election Commission — which party?
Shiv Sena (UBT): Political party in Maharashtra, India. Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) (ISO: Śiva Sēnā (Uddhava Bāḷāsāhēba Ṭhākare); lit. 'Army of Shivaji, led by Uddhav Thackeray'; abbr.
Sparked in 1898 by the sinking of the USS Maine in Havana Harbor, this brief conflict handed the U.S. control of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines — what was it?
Spanish–American War: 1898 conflict between Spain and the United States.
Known by the art name Unam, this authoritarian leader served as South Korea's first president from 1948 until his resignation in 1960?
Syngman Rhee: President of South Korea from 1948 to 1960. Born in Hwanghae Province during the Joseon period, Rhee attended a local Methodist school, where he converted to Christianity.
The eldest son of a US president, this brigadier general received the Medal of Honor for directing troops at Utah Beach during the Normandy landings — who is he?
Theodore Roosevelt Jr.: American general and politician (1887–1944)
Hailed by the Senate as "the best ruler" and counted among the Five Good Emperors, this Hispania-born soldier pushed Rome to its greatest-ever territorial extent. Which emperor?
Trajan: Roman emperor from AD 98 to 117.
Born in Jaffna, this guerrilla leader founded and led a militant organization in a decades-long campaign for an independent Tamil state in Sri Lanka — who is he?
Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine
Velupillai Prabhakaran: Leader of militant Tamil organisation in Sri Lanka (1954–2009)
After rising through China's banking sector to become mayor of Beijing, this retired official later led the Communist Party's anti-corruption watchdog from 2012 to 2017 — who is he?
Wang Qishan: Vice President of China from 2018 to 2023.
Known as "Bill," this British field marshal led the so-called "forgotten army" in the Burma campaign before later serving as governor-general of Australia — who was he?
William Slim, 1st Viscount Slim: British Army field marshal, Governor-General of Australia, and author (1891–1970)

This Israeli politician served as defense minister from 2022 until his dismissal by the prime minister in November 2024, having earlier held posts including construction, immigration, and education minister after starting out in the navy. Who is he?
Yoav Gallant: Israeli politician & military officer (born 1958)
Who wrote The Emperor's New Clothes?

The Emperor's New Clothes → Hans Christian Andersen. The tale has been translated into over 100 languages.
"The Emperor's New Clothes" was first published with "The Little Mermaid" in Copenhagen, Denmark, by C.
Which of these people was born first?
Jabir ibn Hayyan (born 721) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Ellen Swallow Richards (born 1842) is the earliest of the four. Richards graduated from Westford Academy (second oldest secondary school in Massachusetts) in 1862.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Henrietta Swan Leavitt is an astronomer. Henrietta Swan Leavitt (July 4, 1868 – December 12, 1921) was an American astronomer.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Augustus De Morgan is a mathematician. Augustus De Morgan (27 June 1806 – 18 March 1871) was a British mathematician and logician.
What is the atomic number of Technetium?
Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
What is the atomic number of Sulfur?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
In what year was Paul Allen born?
Paul Allen: Paul Gardner Allen (January 21, 1953 – October 15, 2018) was an American businessman, computer programmer, and investor.
In what year was Arthur Schopenhauer born?
Arthur Schopenhauer (22 February 1788 – 21 September 1860) was a German philosopher and writer.
In what year was Lex Fridman born?
Lex Fridman: Alexei "Lex" Fridman (born 15 August 1983) is an American computer scientist and podcaster.
In what year did Mario Molina die?
Mario Molina: Mario José Molina-Pasquel Henríquez (19 March 1943 – 7 October 2020) was a Mexican physical chemist.
In what year did Edward Teller die?
Edward Teller: Born in Austria-Hungary in 1908, Teller emigrated to the US in the 1930s, one of the many so-called "Martians", a group of Hungarian scientist émigrés.
In what year was Möbius strip discovered?
Möbius strip: In mathematics, a Möbius strip, Möbius band, or Möbius loop is a surface that can be formed by attaching the ends of a strip of paper together with a half-twist.
R (programming language): Robert Gentleman. R is a programming language for statistical computing and data visualization.
Prunus domestica: People's Republic of China. Prunus domestica is a species of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.
In which country is IAI Kfir?
Who is credited with discovering Eta Carinae?
Eta Carinae: Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser. It became the second-brightest star in the night sky between 11–14 March 1843 before fading well below naked-eye visibility after 1856.
Who is credited with discovering Benzene?
Benzene: Michael Faraday. Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
Who is credited with discovering Vanadium?
Vanadium: Andrés Manuel del Río. Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.

This British Formula One engineer, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest designers, has served as technical chief at Williams, McLaren, and Red Bull, and now co-owns Aston Martin's F1 team — who is he?
Adrian Newey (born 26 December 1958) is a British engineer, aerodynamicist, automotive designer, and motorsport executive.

Caused by brain damage, disease, or sometimes sedative drugs, this condition splits into a retrograde type that erases memories before an event and an anterograde type that blocks new ones from forming — what is it called?
Amnesia is a deficit in memory caused by brain damage or brain diseases, but it can also be temporarily caused by the use of various sedative and hypnotic drugs.

Sitting at the milder end of a spectrum of diminished motivation — less severe than abulia and far short of akinetic mutism — this is a state marked by an absence of feeling, interest, or concern. What is it?
Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, and/or concern about something.
Originally built by Hawker Siddeley and still produced under license in India today, this subsonic British trainer aircraft equips the Red Arrows aerobatic team — which jet?
BAE Systems Hawk is a British single-engine, subsonic, jet-powered advanced trainer aircraft.

This scientific discipline, a hybrid of chemistry and biology, studies the chemical processes occurring within living organisms and is generally divided into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism — what's the field called?
Biochemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.
Present in both sexes from the same embryonic tissue, these two prominences on the upper torso permanently enlarge only in human females at puberty, driven by estrogen and growth hormone - name them?
Breast are two prominences located on the upper ventral region of the torso in humans and other primates.
Discovered in 1940, this non-intoxicating compound extracted from cannabis is used medically as an anticonvulsant for two rare, severe forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?
Cannabidiol (CBD) is a phytocannabinoid, one of 113 identified cannabinoids in Cannabis, along with tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), and accounts for up to 40% of the plant's extract.
First cultivated in Mesoamerica and later spread worldwide during the Columbian Exchange, this edible gourd-family plant is also known as christophine, mirliton, or choko — what is it?

Chayote (previously placed in the obsolete genus Sechium, now in the genus Sicyos, as Sicyos edulis), also known as christophine, mirliton, gisquil, and choko, is an edible plant belonging to the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae.
Its glorious blue in glass and paint was long wrongly blamed on bismuth, and frustrated miners named its ore after a goblin. Which hard, gray element carries the symbol Co?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Which vanilla-scented, benzopyrone lactone compound acts as a plant's chemical defense against predators and, via its derivatives, gave rise to the anticoagulant warfarin?
Coumarin is an aromatic organic chemical compound with formula C9H6O2.
The word names both a noun — a plan or proposal made by a thinking agent — and a verb for developing one, always aiming to satisfy goals while weighing function and aesthetics; what is it?
Design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system.
Most of the 68 species sharing this name live in Eurasia and Africa, with only two found in North America — and "true" ones are merely a subfamily; what bird is it?
Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?

First recognised in the 1950s but not formally defined until 1990, this disorder of widespread chronic pain — often with fatigue and memory trouble — has no known cause and is treated multidisciplinarily. What is it?
Fibromyalgia (FM) is a long-term condition characterised by widespread chronic pain.
With about 37 species ranging from central Canada down to Costa Rica, this slender, keeled-scaled reptile typically sports longitudinal stripes in blue, yellow, or red — which reptile is it?
Garter snake is the common name for small to medium-sized snakes belonging to the genus Thamnophis in the family Colubridae.
This applied art and academic discipline uses text and images to craft visual communications aimed at specific audiences and objectives — what field is it?
Graphic design is a profession, academic discipline and applied art that involves creating visual communications intended to transmit specific messages to social groups, with specific objectives.
Credited with putting middle-class Americans behind the wheel, this industrialist lent his surname to the very philosophy of assembly-line manufacturing. Who is he?
Henry Ford (July 30, 1863 - April 7, 1947) was an American industrialist and business magnate.
Classified under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5, this condition causes a lack of alertness during waking hours despite — or because of — too much sleep. What is it?
Hypersomnia is a neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness.
Whose 1687 book Principia Mathematica achieved the first great unification in physics and established classical mechanics?

Nicknamed 'Marvellous Merchiston,' this Scottish laird and mathematician popularised the decimal point and invented a set of calculating 'bones' — but he's best known for discovering what underlies the slide rule. Who was he?
John Napier (Latinized as Ioannes Neper; 1 February 1550 - 4 April 1617), nicknamed Marvellous Merchiston, was a Scottish landowner known as a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.
When the natural curve of the thoracic spine exceeds about 45 degrees, doctors give this excessive rounding of the upper back a name rooted in the Greek word for 'hump' — what is it?
Kyphosis (from Greek (kyphos) 'hump') is an abnormally excessive convex curvature of the spine as it occurs in the thoracic and sacral regions.
Born in 1880, this Australian therapist and part-time stage actor is remembered for coaching a stammering British monarch — who is he?
Lionel Logue (26 February 1880 - 12 April 1953) was an Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor who helped King George VI manage his stammer.

An engineer and teacher from a poor family who once served as mayor of Tehran, this politician became Iran's sixth president in 2005 and was a fierce proponent of the country's nuclear program — who is he?
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (n Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.
This natural biological transition marks the permanent end of menstrual periods, typically occurring between ages 45 and 55 as estrogen levels decline — what is it?
Menopause is the time when menstrual periods permanently stop, marking the end of the reproductive stage for the female human.

Caused by a poxvirus spread through direct contact, this viral skin infection produces small raised pink lesions with a distinctive dimple in the center, usually clearing on its own within a year — name the condition?
Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.
This flexible body part lets the head turn in every direction while its compartments guard the spinal cord and upper airway between head and torso — what is it, also known as the cervix?
Neck is the part of the body in many vertebrates that connects the head to the torso.
This insect order includes dragonflies and damselflies, the bulkier ones holding wings out at rest while the slender ones fold theirs along the body — what is it?
Odonata is an order of predatory flying insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies (as well as the Epiophlebia damsel-dragonflies).
Contrasted with 'normophilic' interests and famously tallied at up to 549 types by Anil Aggrawal, this contested clinical category covers atypical sexual attraction — what's its name?
Paraphilia is an uncommon, intense, and persistent sexual arousal or attraction to anything not sexual by nature, though preference is favored for specific designations.
Written by the Hong sisters, this South Korean series about young mages dealing with heaven and earth aired on tvN in two parts during 2022 and 2023. What show is it?
Pharynx (pl.: pharynges) is the part of the throat behind the mouth and nasal cavity, and above the esophagus and trachea (the tubes going down to the stomach and the lungs respectively).
Cough, chest pain, fever, and trouble breathing point to this infection of the lungs' alveoli, often classified by where it was caught — community or hospital — what is it?
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.
This rose-family genus of roughly 340 species includes almonds, apricots, and cherries, whose pit encloses a kernel that's edible in some species and poisonous in others — which genus?

Prunus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs from the family Rosaceae, with about 340 accepted species (as of March 2024) that include peaches and nectarines, apricots, plums, cherries and almonds.
Belonging to the genus Ribes and native to western Europe, which berry carries the scientific name Ribes rubrum and has spread into the wild in many regions?
Redcurrant (Ribes rubrum) is a member of the genus Ribes in the family Grossulariaceae.
Sitting in group 4 just below hafnium, this synthetic element named for a famous physicist has a most-stable isotope that survives only about 48 minutes — which element is it?
Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, this term describes an unplanned fortunate discovery, as with penicillin or the microwave oven — what is it called?
Serendipity is an unplanned fortunate discovery. The concept is often associated with scientific and technological breakthroughs, where accidental discoveries led to new insights or inventions.
This Polish-American Gestalt psychologist insisted 'most social acts lose meaning if isolated' — a credo that shaped his famous experiments on conformity and impression formation. Who was he?
Solomon Asch (September 14, 1907 - February 20, 1996) was a Polish-American Gestalt psychologist and pioneer in social psychology.
This artificial sweetener is produced by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and is roughly 600 times sweeter than sucrose — three times sweeter even than aspartame — what's the sweetener called?

Sucralose is an artificial sweetener and sugar substitute. The commercial success of sucralose-based products stems from its favorable comparison to other low-calorie sweeteners in terms of taste, stability, and safety.
A colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether and a versatile solvent, this compound is mainly used as a precursor to polymers and is an isomer of butanone — what is it?
Tetrahydrofuran (THF), or oxolane, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2)4O.
When water loss to the air outpaces uptake by the roots, plants shut tiny leaf pores to conserve moisture, slowing this evaporative water-movement process — what's it called?
Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, such as leaves, stems and flowers.

Named after an 18th-century Italian physicist and first published in 1797, this phenomenon explains why fluid pressure drops as it speeds up through a narrower pipe section — powering wine aerators and vacuum ejectors. What is it called?
Venturi effect is the reduction in fluid pressure that results when a moving fluid speeds up as it is funneled from one section of a pipe to another, smaller section.
Chairman of the Polish People's Party since 2015 and a former Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, this physician-turned-politician ran for the Polish presidency in 2020 — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (born 10 August 1981) is a Polish physician and politician, who has served as the Deputy Prime Minister of Poland, and Minister of National Defence since 2023.
The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas packs all four of its atoms into one straight line thanks to a carbon-carbon triple bond, and fuels welding torches — which compound is it?
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this soft-spoken economist logged the second-longest tenure ever as chairman of the Federal Reserve — who was he?
Alan Greenspan: American economist and financial advisor (born 1926)
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.
Developed to herd livestock across rough terrain by nipping at their heels, this short-coated working breed's coat reads as either 'red' or 'blue' — which breed?

Australian Cattle Dog: Breed of herding dog. The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
Long-tailed and originally from the Indian subcontinent, this whiskered rodent is a major agricultural pest yet is honored as sacred at the Karni Mata Temple in India — which species is it?
Black rat: Species of rodent. It is a generalist omnivore that can live on a wide variety of foods.
Distinguished by a cube-shaped body, this class of stinging cnidarians includes species such as Chironex fleckeri, whose venom is often fatal to humans — what is it?
Box jellyfish: Class of cnidarians distinguished by their cube-shaped medusae.
Designed in 1959 and partly based on Grace Hopper's FLOW-MATIC, this English-like programming language still runs mainframe banking systems today — what is it?
COBOL: Programming language with English-like syntax.
This involuntary, striated tissue forms the thick middle layer of the heart wall, with individual cells joined by structures called intercalated discs — what is it?
Cardiac muscle: Muscular tissue of heart in vertebrates.

Making up the brain's outer layer of neural tissue, this six-layered structure handles attention, memory, language, and consciousness, and is folded to fit more surface area inside the skull — what is it called?
Cerebral cortex: Outer layer of the cerebrum of the mammalian brain.

An essential nutrient your liver can only partly produce on its own, this compound builds phospholipids in cell membranes and helps make a neurotransmitter for muscle control, and occurs naturally in eggs, meat, and fish — which nutrient?
Choline: Chemical compound and essential nutrient. Choline is a cation with the chemical formula [(CH3)3NCH2CH2OH]+.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family and native to Australia, this crested pet bird is kept in an estimated 4.8 million US households — what bird is it?
Cockatiel: Species of bird. It is, therefore, now classified as the smallest subfamily of the Cacatuidae (cockatoo family).
Nicknamed the shaggy mane or lawyer's wig, this scaly white mushroom dissolves itself into black ink just hours after being picked — which fungus?
Coprinus comatus: Species of fungus. The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.
Sold under trade names like Super Glue and Krazy Glue, this fast-acting adhesive family rapidly polymerizes the moment it contacts water — which chemical group?
Cyanoacrylate: Type of fast-acting adhesive. The cyanoacrylate group in the monomer rapidly polymerizes in the presence of water to form long, strong chains.
With evidence of practice dating back to 7000 BC, this field is considered the very first specialization to branch off from general medicine — what is it?
Dentistry: Branch of medicine. Dentistry, also known as dental medicine and oral medicine, is the branch of medicine focused on the teeth, gums, and mouth.
Nicknamed 'Spad' after a World War I fighter, this piston-engine attack plane flew from 1946 into the 1980s, an anachronism deep into the Jet Age — which aircraft?
Douglas A-1 Skyraider: American single engine attack aircraft.
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Also called slapped cheek syndrome, this common childhood illness is caused by parvovirus B19, discovered in 1975 — what condition is it?
Fifth disease: Red rash due to infection with parvovirus B19.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?
This field studies how geography shapes international relations and foreign policy, though critics have dismissed its early theories as pseudoscience — which discipline?
Geopolitics: Study of geography's effects on politics.
This plant genus in the mallow family gives us cotton, humanity's primary natural fiber, with its name tracing to an Arabic word for a soft substance — which genus?
Gossypium: Genus of flowering plants in the mallow family Malvaceae.

Derived independently in the 1830s by two European researchers and later given theoretical backing by George Stokes, this law describes the pressure drop of laminar flow through a drinking straw or a hypodermic needle — what's it called?
Hagen–Poiseuille equation: Law describing the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid.

Governed by rules laid out in a document called a blazon, this medieval discipline of coats of arms, crests, and mottoes may have arisen so knights could recognize commanders behind their helmets — what is it?
Heraldry: Discipline of the design and study of coats of arms.
Running from your shoulder to your elbow, this long arm bone has a constriction nicknamed the 'surgical neck' due to its tendency to fracture — which bone?
Humerus: Long bone of the upper arm. It connects the scapula and the two bones of the lower arm, the radius and ulna, and consists of three sections.

Trained originally as a naval architect before becoming a self-taught nuclear physicist, this scientist directed the Soviet Union's atomic bomb program and earned the nickname 'father of the Russian bomb' — who is he?
This tech entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, later built a fintech company behind Square, Cash App, and Tidal, and also helped launch the decentralized network Bluesky?
This English scientist's 1808 book, 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy,' laid the foundations of modern atomic theory, and he also kept daily weather records for over fifty years — who was he?
John Dalton: British chemist and physicist (1766–1844)
Patented in 1967 and approved for medical use in 1980, this propionic-acid-class NSAID works by blocking prostaglandin production — what is it?
Known by common names like true lavender and English lavender despite not being native to England, this Mediterranean-basin plant belongs to the mint family — which species?
Lavandula angustifolia: Species of plant. Lavandula angustifolia, formerly L. officinalis, is a flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to the Mediterranean basin.
Also known as the deer ked, this blood-sucking fly sheds its own wings once it lands on a host and burrows through the fur to feed — what species is it?
Lipoptena cervi: Species of fly. Lipoptena cervi, the deer ked or deer fly, is a species of biting fly in the family of louse flies, Hippoboscidae.
This common, nonspecific medical sign involves lymph nodes becoming abnormally swollen or enlarged, with causes ranging from the common cold to cancer. What's the condition called?
Lymphadenopathy: Abnormal change in size of the lymph nodes.
A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered the element francium in 1939 and later became the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Typically running 21 to 35 days, this coordinated dance of estrogen and progesterone prepares the uterine lining and releases an egg to make pregnancy possible — what is it?
Menstrual cycle: Natural changes in the human female reproductive system.
Known to NATO as 'Flogger,' this Soviet variable-sweep-wing fighter was the first in the country's air force to carry look-down/shoot-down radar, with over 5,000 built. Which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet fighter-interceptor aircraft introduced in 1970.
Drawn from the latex of opium poppies, this naturally occurring opiate acts straight on the central nervous system to dull pain — but risks dependence and tolerance. What is it?
Morphine: Pain medication of the opiate family.
This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, bringing on excessive daytime sleepiness, sleep paralysis, and sudden episodes of muscle collapse called cataplexy — what is it?
Narcolepsy: Human sleep disorder. Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep–wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.

Usually made from unleavened dough that's rolled, cut, or extruded into long strips, this staple food is called pasta in Italian cuisine and split into wheat-based and starch-based varieties in Chinese cooking — what is it?
Noodle: Staple food made from unleavened dough, commonly long and thin.

Born out of military planning before World War II, this branch of applied mathematics uses optimization and statistics to find the best possible outcome for real-world decisions — what field, sometimes called management science?
Operations research: Discipline concerning the application of advanced analytical methods.
Also called the corn poppy or Flanders poppy, this red flowering weed has symbolized remembrance in the Commonwealth since World War I — what plant is it?
Papaver rhoeas: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.
This term describes a short chain of amino acids joined by a particular kind of bond; string together enough of them (10,000 daltons or more) and you get a protein instead — what is it?
Peptide: Short chains of 2–50 amino acids.
Cultivated since the days of the Inca Empire and known in English as the Cape gooseberry or goldenberry, this South American nightshade now grows wild worldwide — which species is it?
Physalis peruviana: Species of cultivated South American fruit. Physalis peruviana is a species of plant in the nightshade family (Solanaceae) native to Chile and Peru.

Derived from renewable resources such as corn starch and capable of biodegrading, this thermoplastic polyester made up about a quarter of the world's bioplastic market in 2022 — what compound is this?
This deciduous member of the rose family includes many varieties known as plums in English, with greengages and damsons among its subspecies — which species is it?
Prunus domestica: Species of flowering plant.

Historically nicknamed 'hydrophobia' because sufferers panic at the offer of a drink, this viral disease causes severe brain inflammation and is virtually always fatal once symptoms appear. What is it?
Rabies: Deadly viral disease, transmitted through animals.
Nicknamed golden root or Arctic root, this Crassulaceae plant is popular in herbal supplements even though the FDA has warned sellers against overselling its health benefits — which plant?
Rhodiola rosea: Species of flowering plant in the stonecrop family.
A synthetic element named for a famous physicist, it's the first of the super-heavy transactinides and behaves chemically as the heavier cousin of hafnium in group 4 — which element?
Rutherfordium: Chemical element with atomic number 104 (Rf)
Nicknamed 'Devil's Breath' and derived from nightshade plants, which motion-sickness drug has also been used historically as a deliriant?
Named for its enormous footwear-shaped beak, this large wading bird of East African swamps was once classified with storks but is now grouped with pelicans and herons — what is it?
Shoebill: Species of bird. The shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird.
After designing the BBC Micro and its BASIC, this English computer scientist co-created the instruction set for ARM — now the most widely used processor architecture in smartphones. Who is she?
Common in coastal tropical waters worldwide, this group of cartilaginous fish includes about 220 species across 29 genera, from butterfly rays to manta and devil rays — what are they?

Located near the border of two constellations some 18.2 billion light-years away, this hyperluminous quasar harbors one of the most massive black holes ever found, at roughly 40 billion solar masses — what is it?
TON 618: Quasar and Lyman-alpha blob in the constellations of Canes Venatici and Coma Berenices.
